overall_summary: Deduplication of the observational data reveals that extreme cosmic and planetary curiosity hooks (specifically 'What If' scenarios about extreme planets and unique planetary anomalies) dominate engagement velocity and viewer retention, generating the highest view counts and like-per-view ratios over the recent 7-day performance window.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) garnered high view velocity (around 1,000 views) and strong like ratios (up to 38 likes) within days of release.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on hypothetical space disaster/immersion scenarios involving exotic, deadly, or high-value worlds.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing surreal phenomena such as 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (A9Qa-RmuOr0) and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (v1rrcZLdp4U) drove over 1,000 views and consistent engagement without relying on clickbait.
winning_patterns.action: Continue producing short-form content highlighting counter-intuitive space and planetary facts with clean numerical or spatial extremes.

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics centered around personal psychology and memory (e.g., 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories', 2fqaGqfsR4A, r43-7nSn8SQ) flatlined with minimal views (5-10 views) and zero engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize psychological micro-facts and redirect content resources toward high-performing space and strange science niches.

weak_patterns.pattern: Stale Animal Facts Without Extinction or Scale Hooks
weak_patterns.evidence: Standard animal facts like 'The Only Animal That Can Live Forever' (F1kXwuXuNgo) or general brain functions lagged significantly behind space content in velocity.
weak_patterns.action: Shift animal content exclusively toward cinematic survival or high-scale historical anomalies rather than standard biology.
